question: Why are women biologically more at risk of getting STIs than men?

options.A: The rapid turnover rate of vaginal epithelial cells
options.B: The large area of delicate mucosal tissue in the female reproductive tract
options.C: Lower natural antibody counts in female sweat
options.D: A higher resting internal body temperature in the pelvis

explanation: The fragile lining inside the female reproductive tract easily forms tiny micro-tears during sex, giving germs an easy way to enter the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is it tricky that many STIs in women show no symptoms at all?

options.A: The immune system permanently attacks healthy tissues instead of the pathogen
options.B: Infected women unknowingly spread the infection and delay necessary treatment
options.C: Routine diagnostic tests consistently fail to detect silent infections
options.D: Asymptomatic infections immediately progress to systemic organ failure

explanation: When an infection causes no signs or pain, a woman has no reason to visit the clinic, letting the disease grow quietly and pass to others. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: What do we call passing an STI from a mother to her baby during childbirth?
explanation: Vertical transmission simply means passing an infection from mother to child during pregnancy, labor, or delivery. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: What happens during an 'ascending infection' in the female reproductive system?

options.A: Pathogens move upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes
options.B: Viruses migrate from skin lesions down to the regional lymph nodes
options.C: Fungi multiply rapidly on the external vulva and travel to the bladder
options.D: Bacteria travel through the bloodstream directly to the heart valves

explanation: An ascending infection is just germs traveling upward—moving past the cervix and into the upper reproductive organs where they can cause serious trouble. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the name of the painless sore that shows up during the first stage of syphilis?
explanation: The classic early sign of syphilis is a firm, round, usually painless sore called a chancre right where the bacteria entered the skin. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h3)

question: A young female patient has Chlamydia. What is the standard medical treatment?

options.A: A series of therapeutic vaccines given over a six-month recovery period
options.B: Strict bed rest and immune-boosting vitamins with no prescription medications
options.C: A course of oral antibiotics for the patient and treatment for her recent sexual partners
options.D: Surgical drainage of infected cervical cysts followed by topical anti-fungals

explanation: Chlamydia is caused by bacteria, so it needs antibiotics! Always remember to treat sexual partners too, otherwise, they'll just pass it right back. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which viral STI is managed with lifelong antivirals to keep painful blisters under control?
explanation: Herpes simplex causes flare-ups of painful blisters. Antivirals don't cure the virus completely, but they help manage and shorten the outbreaks. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why do high-risk strains of HPV require regular cervical screening even when a woman feels fine?

options.A: High-risk HPV can cause silent cellular changes in the cervix that lead to cancer over time
options.B: Routine screening is the only way to clear the virus completely from nerve tissues
options.C: HPV bacteria become resistant to standard antibiotic therapies if left unchecked
options.D: The virus rapidly destroys red blood cells and causes severe systemic anemia

explanation: High-risk HPV can change cervical cells without causing any pain or warning signs. That's why routine Pap smears are so lifesaving! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: What type of germ causes trichomoniasis?
explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny, swimming parasite known as *Trichomonas vaginalis*. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which symptom helps tell a yeast infection apart from trichomoniasis?

options.A: A painless firm chancre on the external labia
options.B: Frothy, yellow-green discharge with a strong, fishy smell
options.C: Painful, fluid-filled vesicles that rupture into open ulcers
options.D: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with no foul odor

explanation: Yeast infections (candidiasis) usually bring thick, white discharge and intense itching, unlike the frothy, foul-smelling discharge of trichomoniasis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main laboratory test used to detect chlamydia and gonorrhea from a swab or urine sample?
explanation: NAATs are the gold standard! They accurately copy and spot tiny amounts of the germ's genetic material. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: A patient looks very anxious while preparing for a pelvic exam for lower belly pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Skip the speculum exam entirely and prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics without testing
options.B: Insist she lie back immediately to keep the clinic schedule running on time
options.C: Explain each step of the procedure calmly and reassure her about privacy and comfort
options.D: Ask a security guard to stand in the room until the examination is finished

explanation: As a nurse, your warmth and clear explanations help ease patient fears, build trust, and make the clinical exam go much smoother. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time when someone has a bacterial STI?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory insurance claim covers the cost of the initial diagnostic workup
options.B: To speed up the metabolic clearance of the antibiotic through the kidneys
options.C: To prevent the patient from becoming immediately reinfected after finishing treatment
options.D: To prevent the development of drug-resistant fungal strains in the community

explanation: Treating partners simultaneously stops the back-and-forth 'ping-pong' spread of the infection between couples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: What key advice should you give a patient being treated for a new sexually transmitted infection?

options.A: Abstain from sexual intercourse until medication is finished and symptoms resolve
options.B: Share remaining prescription pills with friends who report similar symptoms
options.C: Stop taking the prescribed antibiotics as soon as the physical itching stops
options.D: Avoid drinking clean water for forty-eight hours after taking oral medication

explanation: Taking a break from sex during treatment lets the body heal fully and stops the infection from being passed around again. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: What major reproductive problem is linked to fallopian tube scarring from untreated pelvic infections?
explanation: Scars in the fallopian tubes can block eggs from traveling normally, leading either to trouble getting pregnant or dangerous ectopic pregnancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)

question: How does an untreated lower genital infection turn into Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Fungi colonize the bladder wall and obstruct the normal flow of urine
options.B: Bacteria enter the systemic circulation and settle permanently in the heart valves
options.C: Pathogens ascend from the cervix through the uterus into the fallopian tubes and pelvic cavity
options.D: Viruses alter bone marrow production, leading to severe immunological suppression

explanation: PID happens when bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix, causing widespread inflammation in the upper reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)

question: What is one of the best everyday ways to teach patients to lower their risk of catching STIs?

options.A: Underlining the importance of monthly pelvic ultrasound scans
options.B: Taking daily prophylactic doses of strong broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Avoiding all physical contact with family members in public settings
options.D: Consistent and correct use of barrier methods like condoms

explanation: Barrier methods create a physical block that stops infectious fluids from passing during sex, offering great protection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h9)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to offer non-judgmental counseling when discussing sexual health?

options.A: It legally waives the hospital from liability during invasive pelvic examinations
options.B: It builds trust, encouraging patients to share accurate health history and seek timely care
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will never contract a viral infection in the future
options.D: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing during clinical visits

explanation: When patients feel judged or shamed, they hide their symptoms and avoid clinics. A warm, open approach keeps them safe and cared for! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h9)
